title: India Chases Cricket Gold as Sindhu Leads Packed Asian Games Day 4 Schedule
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's women face Sri Lanka for T20 gold at 10:30 AM IST on September 22, while PV Sindhu's badminton squad meets hosts Japan and shooters Parth Mane and Elavenil Valarivan target a medal.
body:
• September 22 is the busiest day of India's Asian Games 2026 campaign so far: the women's cricket team faces Sri Lanka in the gold-medal match at 10:30 AM IST at Korogi Athletic Park.
  • PV Sindhu leads the women's badminton team against hosts Japan in the quarter-final at 6:00 AM IST at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium; the men's team, featuring Lakshya Sen and HS Prannoy, also plays Japan at 11:30 AM IST.
  • Shooters Parth Rakesh Mane and Elavenil Valarivan contest the 10m air rifle mixed team event, with qualification at 6:15 AM IST and the medal match at 8:25 AM IST. Skeet qualification rounds also run through the day.
  • The schedule also includes wushu medal action, men's hockey against Sri Lanka at 3:30 PM, men's kabaddi against South Korea at 7:15 AM, and women's table tennis against Thailand at 6:30 AM.

Cricket gold on the line

The day's headline event arrives at 10:30 AM IST (2:00 PM JST), when Harmanpreet Kaur's India takes on Sri Lanka in the women's T20 gold-medal match. India booked the final with a dominant 114-run semifinal victory, and enters as defending champion — the team won the women's cricket title at the previous Games in Hangzhou. A gold on Tuesday would open India's medal account in style and set the tone for the fortnight in Aichi-Nagoya.

"A dominant 114-run victory for #TeamIndia. They are all set to face Sri Lanka next in the Gold Medal match."

— BCCI Women, on X

The squad is at full strength for the final, with Smriti Mandhana deputising, Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma in the middle order, and Richa Ghosh behind the stumps, according to the announced tournament squad.

Sindhu leads the badminton charge

Action begins early — very early for viewers in India. At 6:00 AM IST (9:30 AM JST), the women's badminton team led by PV Sindhu faces hosts Japan in the quarter-final. Sindhu is joined by Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag, Tanvi Sharma and Isharani Baruah, with the doubles pairings of Treesa and Gayatri adding depth. Japan at home is a formidable draw, and a win would put India one step from a team medal.

The men follow at 11:30 AM IST (3:00 PM JST), also against Japan in their quarter-final. The squad packs experience: Lakshya Sen, Ayush Shetty, HS Prannoy and Kidambi Srikanth, backed by the world-class doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. Both ties are scheduled at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.

Shooters take aim

Shooting could deliver India's first medals of the morning. Parth Rakesh Mane and Elavenil Valarivan pair up in the 10m air rifle mixed team event — qualification at 6:15 AM IST, with the medal round at 8:25 AM IST. India's shooters have been among the country's most reliable medal sources at multi-sport Games, and a podium here would be the day's earliest prize.

The skeet ranges are busy too: Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan feature in the men's individual and team qualification rounds, while Parinaaz Dhaliwal, Raiza Dhillon and Maheshwari Chauhan contest the women's skeet qualification, according to ANI's schedule report.

Across the venues

Wushu offers another early medal shot: Hanjabam Langlentombi Devi competes in the women's nandatu final at 6:29 AM IST, with Roshibina Devi fighting the women's 60kg quarter-final around 3:15 PM. The men's hockey team, a perennial medal contender, opens its Pool A campaign against Sri Lanka at 3:30 PM, while the men's kabaddi team — champions at Hangzhou 2023 — begins its group stage against South Korea at 7:15 AM.

The women's table tennis team meets Thailand in the pre-quarter-final at 6:30 AM IST. Further down the schedule: boxing's Jadumani Singh faces Nepal's Chandra Bahadur Thapa in the men's 55kg round of 32 at 10:30 AM, Aadhya Tiwari takes on Thailand's Alisha Ziegler in women's singles soft tennis at 5:30 AM, and India's men's sepaktakraw team plays Malaysia at the same hour. Boxing, fencing, swimming, equestrian, karate and esports fill out the rest of the contingent's day.

What to watch

For the Indian diaspora in Japan — and fans streaming back home — Day 4 is the first true litmus test of the campaign. A cricket gold, a badminton upset over the hosts, or a shooting medal would give India early momentum before the track, wrestling and boxing medal rounds begin. All times are subject to change per the official schedule.
image_caption: PV Sindhu at a felicitation ceremony after her Olympic silver medal. Sindhu faces Japan in her Asian Games 2026 badminton tie on September 22.
nri_angle: Indian fans in Japan and streaming worldwide get their first full day of medal action, with the cricket final at a diaspora-friendly mid-morning IST slot.
